meta.title: The Spy Who Fooled an Entire Country
meta.working_title: The Spy Who Fooled an Entire Country (Eli Cohen, Part 1)
meta.device: The radio key. A small Morse key hidden in a tea tin keeps returning: we hear its tapping under scene changes, see it in training in Israel, packed in a suitcase in Buenos Aires, and in the last shot under the window of a Damascus apartment across the street from army headquarters. Part 2 opens with the same key.
meta.style: 2D dynamic, locked Village Painterly look: 6-head characters from the village-cast rig in 1950s-60s dress (Alexandria linen suits, Israeli army khaki, Buenos Aires tailored suits and hats, Damascus officers in olive uniforms and berets, party guests in cocktail clothes). Eli Cohen keeps one face sheet with a thin moustache. Highly detailed painted backgrounds with warm light and dynamic cast shadows: Alexandria's corniche, a Cairo police cell, a Tel Aviv flat, a training safehouse with maps, a Buenos Aires café, Damascus rooftops, the Hamidiyah souk, an apartment opposite army HQ. Moving cameras, 3 to 5 parallax layers, characters act in every shot. Neutral tone on Israel and Syria. SFX under VO (Morse tapping is the motif); music at combine.
meta.source: 'Israeli Spy Who Almost Became Syria's President' (Pushpam upload, batch 5, Hindi, Nitish Rajput). Translated, fully rewritten in our own words and fact-checked; split into 2 parts. Part 1: Alexandria to the 1963 coup.

shots.vo: Damascus, the early 1960s. A rich businessman throws parties for army officers, ministers and their friends. Everyone likes Kamel Amin Thaabet.
shots.visual: A rooftop party at night: officers in uniform, men in suits, music, a smiling host with a thin moustache raising a glass.
shots.anim: Lanterns sway; glasses clink; the host laughs.

shots.vo: After the guests leave, he goes to his bedroom, opens a tin of tea, and takes out a radio key.
shots.visual: The empty party room; then a bedroom: the host lifts a false bottom from a tea tin and connects a small Morse key to wires.
shots.anim: The tin lid twists off; a wire clicks into place.

shots.vo: The messages go to Israel. Kamel Amin Thaabet does not exist. His real name is Eli Cohen.
shots.visual: Close on his finger tapping the key; the dots and dashes turn into a line across a map from Damascus to Tel Aviv.
shots.anim: Tapping sound; the line draws itself.

shots.visual: Title over the tea tin on a windowsill, Damascus rooftops beyond.
shots.onscreen: THE SPY WHO FOOLED AN ENTIRE COUNTRY
shots.anim: Night breeze moves the curtain; title fades up.

shots.vo: Eliyahu Ben-Shaul Cohen was born in 1924 in Alexandria, Egypt, into a Jewish family whose roots were in Aleppo, in Syria.
shots.visual: Alexandria's corniche in the 1930s: trams, the sea, a family walking; a boy holding his father's hand.
shots.anim: Tram bells; gulls; the boy looks at the sea.

shots.vo: He grew up speaking Arabic like a native, along with French and Hebrew. Teachers said he had a strong memory for detail.
shots.visual: A classroom; the boy reciting from memory while classmates look on.
shots.anim: Chalk dust drifts in the sunlight.

shots.vo: After Israel was founded in 1948, life for Egypt's Jews grew harder. In 1949 his parents and brothers left for Israel. Eli stayed behind.
shots.visual: A harbour: the family boarding a ship; Eli waving from the dock.
shots.anim: The ship's horn; the gap between dock and ship widens.

shots.vo: In Egypt he helped Jews leave in secret. In 1954, after an Israeli sabotage plot in Egypt was uncovered, he was arrested and questioned, but released.
shots.visual: A Cairo police office: Eli sitting calmly under a lamp while an officer shouts; then Eli walking out into the sun.
shots.anim: The lamp swings; the door opens to bright light.

shots.vo: After the Suez war of 1956, Egypt expelled many of its Jews. Eli arrived in Israel in early 1957.
shots.visual: A crowded ship deck; Eli with a small suitcase looking at the Haifa coast.
shots.anim: Waves; the coast grows.

shots.vo: In Israel, he worked as a clerk and translator. In 1959 he married Nadia, and they started a family.
shots.visual: A small flat in Tel Aviv; Eli and Nadia at a table; a baby's cot.
shots.anim: Steam rises from cups; the cot rocks.

shots.vo: He had already been turned down once by Israel's intelligence services. But in 1960 the army's intelligence branch came back to him.
shots.visual: Two men in plain suits at the flat's door; Eli listening; Nadia in the background.
shots.anim: The door opens; one man takes off his hat.

shots.vo: Israel wanted a man inside Syria. Syrian guns on the Golan Heights shelled Israeli farms below, and Israel knew little about what was up there.
shots.visual: A map: the Golan Heights above the Sea of Galilee; Syrian gun positions; Israeli fields below.
shots.anim: Little puffs of shellfire on the map.

shots.vo: For months, he trained: Syrian dialect, the Quran and Muslim prayer, codes, invisible ink, and the radio key.
shots.visual: A safehouse room: Eli practising Morse; then kneeling on a prayer mat with an instructor; then learning to spot weapons from photos.
shots.anim: Morse tapping; photos slide across the table.

shots.vo: They built him a new life: Kamel Amin Thaabet, a Syrian Muslim whose family had moved to Argentina, now a successful businessman who longed to go home.
shots.visual: A desk with a new passport, business cards and family photos being assembled; the name KAMEL AMIN THAABET typed onto a card.
shots.anim: Typewriter keys strike the name.

shots.vo: In 1961 he flew to Buenos Aires, home to a large Syrian and Lebanese community.
shots.visual: Buenos Aires: wide boulevards, an old car, cafés; Eli in a sharp suit stepping out of a taxi.
shots.anim: Traffic; pigeons rise.

shots.vo: He spent months making friends: at cafés, clubs and the Arab-language press. He gave to Syrian causes and spoke passionately about the homeland.
shots.visual: A café full of men in suits; Eli at the centre telling a story; others laughing; a newspaper editor taking notes.
shots.anim: Cigarette smoke curls; laughter.

shots.vo: He also met Syrian officials posted to Argentina. One later account says he got to know Amin al-Hafiz, a military attaché who would soon lead Syria, though Hafiz always denied meeting him there.
shots.visual: An embassy reception; Eli shaking hands with a stocky officer in a uniform with medals.
shots.anim: A camera flash freezes the handshake.

shots.vo: By the time he left, he had letters of introduction to important people in Damascus.
shots.visual: Eli packing a suitcase; envelopes go in; then the tea tin with the radio key slides into a hidden pocket.
shots.anim: The suitcase clicks shut.

shots.vo: In early 1962 he arrived in Damascus.
shots.visual: Damascus from a hill: domes, minarets, the Umayyad Mosque; a car driving into the city.
shots.anim: The call to prayer; the car winds down the road.

shots.vo: He rented an apartment across the street from the army's general headquarters. From his window he could watch who came and went.
shots.visual: An apartment window; across the street, a guarded gate with army trucks; Eli behind the curtain with a notebook.
shots.anim: Trucks roll in; the curtain twitches.

shots.vo: He opened an import-export business, and began to throw parties.
shots.visual: A small office with crates; then a lively party with officers, music and food.
shots.anim: Crates stack up; then the party fills the room.

shots.vo: Officers drank and talked. He listened. Late at night, he tapped out what he had heard to Tel Aviv.
shots.visual: A table of officers talking with their hands; Eli laughing and refilling glasses; then the dark bedroom and the radio key.
shots.anim: Party noise fades into Morse tapping.

shots.vo: Every few months he flew back to Israel through Europe, to see Nadia and his children, who believed he was buying equipment abroad for the government.
shots.visual: A plane at night; then a Tel Aviv kitchen: Eli hugging his small children; Nadia smiling.
shots.anim: Children run into his arms.

shots.vo: Syria in those years was unstable. Governments came and went, often through military coups.
shots.visual: Newspaper front pages stacking up with different leaders' faces.
shots.anim: Pages pile up like cards.

shots.vo: On the eighth of March 1963, officers of the Ba'ath Party seized power.
shots.visual: Tanks in a Damascus square at dawn; soldiers at the radio station; a crowd watching.
shots.anim: Tank tracks clank; a radio tower against the sunrise.

shots.vo: Many of the new men in power were people Kamel had met at his parties. Within months, Amin al-Hafiz became Syria's leader.
shots.visual: A palace hall; officers who were at Eli's parties now in high posts; Amin al-Hafiz at the centre.
shots.anim: Camera pans along familiar faces.

shots.vo: Suddenly, Israel's spy was a friend of the government.
shots.visual: Eli at a party, now with ministers; someone hands him an official invitation with an eagle seal.
shots.anim: He smiles; the seal glints.

shots.vo: Officers began to offer him something no spy could normally get: a tour of the Syrian defences on the Golan Heights.
shots.visual: An army jeep at the foot of the Golan; an officer waving Eli into the passenger seat.
shots.anim: The jeep door swings open; hold on Eli's face. To be continued.

hooks: He partied with Syria's ministers and toured their bunkers on the Golan. He was an Israeli spy.
Kamel Amin Thaabet was the most popular host in Damascus. He did not exist.

fixes: Born 26 Dec 1924, Alexandria; Syrian-Jewish family from Aleppo. Parents emigrated 1949.
1954: Operation Susannah (Lavon affair) exposure; Cohen was detained and questioned but released for lack of evidence. Expelled after Suez, reached Israel Feb 1957.
Married Nadia Majald 1959. First rejected by Mossad (1955); recruited by military intelligence Unit 188 in 1960.
Arrived Buenos Aires Feb 1961; arrived Damascus Jan/Feb 1962. Apartment in Abu Rummaneh opposite the General Staff HQ.
Amin al-Hafiz meeting in Argentina: widely told but Hafiz denied it in later interviews. Script says 'one later account... Hafiz always denied'.
Ba'ath coup 8 March 1963; Hafiz became head of state July 1963.
Source title says he 'almost became Syria's president': a legend. The common, also unconfirmed, claim is he was considered for deputy defence minister; that goes in Part 2 as a rumour only.
Dropped the source's unsourced claims about girlfriends and hidden cameras; sponsor reads cut.
cuts: Part 1 ends at the 1963 coup and the Golan tour invitation. Part 2: the Golan, the eucalyptus trees, capture in Jan 1965, trial, hanging 18 May 1965, the missing remains.
